new.name: The horn
new.what: A horn on one key: a noise that turns heads, calls a fare or a crewman out, and is heard like any act.
new.design: One key sounds the horn while held. It is a noise at a set reach (about 60 m by day, further at night, less in rain) that turns watchers' heads like any noise (2.2.4). A short toot outside a door brings out a fare or a man Tom is waiting for; a long blast in a quiet street at night is remembered as a noise and draws a look from lit windows. Pedestrians in the road step aside; it never alarms police on its own.
new.test: A horn sounded at night is heard by every listener inside its reach and by nobody outside it, and a waiting fare inside 15 m comes out within 10 s (golden rows).

reason: A held key turns the car camera to the rear window (A24).
Ramming, damage by closing speed, nobody inside killed (A24).
Only parked cars are taken, never a car with somebody in it (A27, built to the recommended answer of his question 2; flips if he picks otherwise).
Ordinary fast driving is never stopped (A12, ER-TRAFFIC-02), so there is no law to break by accident and a limiter has no job.

Several keys to every lock: quiet (a key, a back way) or loud force.

Goods taken off a lorry or van are a lift; an armed raid on an armoured cash van stays out (guns rare and late, ruling 18 Nov).
A safe needs its key or combination from a person, never a dial game (A4).

new.name: Lifting from a pocket
new.what: Taking a key, a letter or a wallet from a coat in a crowd or a packed room, as one held press; caught or not by the person's attention.
new.design: Beside or behind a person in a crowd, a queue or a packed caff, one held press of about 2 s takes the one thing worth taking (authored: a key, a letter, a wallet); no minigame. The person may feel it: the chance rises with his attention, the light and how few people are near; felt, it is a deed with the seven slots and he turns on Tom there and then. A lifted key is one of the keys to a lock (1.6.1) and is missed by morning, so the owner knows when it went and who was near him.
new.test: A lift on an attentive person alone in daylight is always felt, one on a distracted person in a crowd of three or more is felt less than one time in four, and a lifted key is missed by the next morning (golden rows).

question: Should Tom be able to lift things from people's pockets? (a) yes, keys, letters and wallets only, as a quiet way into jobs [recommended]; (b) no.

new.name: A torch on a night job
new.what: A hand torch in a pocket: it lights a dark room for searching and shows him to anyone who can see the beam.
new.design: A torch, bought at the ironmonger, takes one of the two pockets under the coat (1.6.9). Switched on, it lights a short cone; searches in a dark room take their table time (A4) with it and twice as long without it. A lit torch makes Tom count at a lit figure's light to anyone with a line of sight to him or the beam, and a beam moving behind a window is seen from the street as a precursor. Off, it is a thing in a pocket a constable may find.
new.test: In the same dark room, a search with the torch takes the table time and without it twice that; a watcher outside the window catches the beam as a precursor only when the torch is on (golden rows).

A film camera would be the 1990 form; the Ledger already writes down what Tom sees (DESIGN 10), so a camera adds nothing to the verbs or the town's memory; canon's smallest budget (DESIGN 18 holds the camcorder to one side story).

A towing job is a vehicle-job sim: not a driving game (canon, DESIGN 18), no taxi-sim parts, and it feeds neither the verbs nor the town's memory (smallest budget).
Fares are named people Pauline calls, going where their routine takes them; no random roadside pickups (DESIGN 18; canon: fares few and chosen).
Sight uses the same bands for Tom and the town (DESIGN 2: shape 35 m, mark 18 m, face 8 m); casing (1.6.11) is done close, which is its risk, and a zoom tool would remove that.
